claim: A bioinformatics pipeline can uncover novel, but rare, riboswitch candidates as well as other noncoding RNA structures in bacteria.
source: We recently implemented a bioinformatics pipeline that can uncover novel, but rare, riboswitch candidates as well as other noncoding RNA structures in bacteria.
evidence: The abstract states this as a direct assertion about the capabilities of their implemented pipeline.

claim: The thiS motif is frequently associated with a gene coding for the ThiS protein.
source: A prominent candidate revealed by our initial search efforts was called the 'thiS motif' because of its frequent association with a gene coding for the ThiS protein, which delivers sulfur to form the thiazole moiety of the thiamin precursor HET-P.
evidence: The abstract explicitly states the association between the thiS motif and the thiS gene.

claim: ThiS protein delivers sulfur to form the thiazole moiety of the thiamin precursor HET-P.
source: A prominent candidate revealed by our initial search efforts was called the 'thiS motif' because of its frequent association with a gene coding for the ThiS protein, which delivers sulfur to form the thiazole moiety of the thiamin precursor HET-P.
evidence: The abstract states the function of ThiS protein based on established knowledge.

claim: thiS motif RNAs function as sensors of the thiamin precursor HMP-PP.
source: In the current report, we describe biochemical and genetic data demonstrating that thiS motif RNAs function as sensors of the thiamin precursor HMP-PP, which is fused with HET-P ultimately to form the final active coenzyme thiamin pyrophosphate (TPP).
evidence: The abstract explicitly states this as a main finding supported by biochemical and genetic data presented in the manuscript.

claim: HMP-PP is fused with HET-P to form the final active coenzyme thiamin pyrophosphate (TPP).
source: In the current report, we describe biochemical and genetic data demonstrating that thiS motif RNAs function as sensors of the thiamin precursor HMP-PP, which is fused with HET-P ultimately to form the final active coenzyme thiamin pyrophosphate (TPP).
evidence: The abstract states this as established biochemical knowledge about TPP biosynthesis.

claim: HMP-PP riboswitches exhibit a distinctive architecture wherein an unusually small ligand-sensing aptamer is almost entirely embedded within an otherwise classic intrinsic transcription terminator stem.
source: HMP-PP riboswitches exhibit a distinctive architecture wherein an unusually small ligand-sensing aptamer is almost entirely embedded within an otherwise classic intrinsic transcription terminator stem.
evidence: The abstract explicitly describes the unique structural architecture of HMP-PP riboswitches.

claim: Bacteria use HMP-PP riboswitches to tune the levels of thiamin precursors during the biosynthesis of TPP.
source: This arrangement yields remarkably compact genetic switches that bacteria use to tune the levels of thiamin precursors during the biosynthesis of this universally distributed coenzyme.
evidence: The abstract states this as a conclusion about the biological function of HMP-PP riboswitches.

claim: Approximately 40 distinct riboswitch classes that regulate gene expression in various bacterial species have been experimentally validated to date.
source: Approximately 40 distinct riboswitch classes that regulate gene expression in various bacterial species have been experimentally validated to date (McCown et al., 2017; Serganov and Nudler, 2013; Sherwood and Henkin, 2016; Breaker, 2011).
evidence: The introduction cites multiple references to support this statement about the number of validated riboswitch classes.

claim: Many thousands of additional riboswitch classes remain to be discovered in the eubacterial domain of life.
source: Based on the abundances and distributions of these known riboswitch classes, it has been proposed that many thousands of additional riboswitch classes remain to be discovered in the eubacterial domain of life (Ames and Breaker, 2010; Breaker, 2012; McCown et al., 2017).
evidence: The introduction cites references supporting this prediction about undiscovered riboswitches.

claim: Known riboswitch classes largely sense compounds or ions that are of fundamental importance to organisms from all three domains of life.
source: The collection of known riboswitch classes largely sense compounds or ions that are of fundamental importance to organisms from all three domains of life, and these ligands also exhibit a bias in favor of compounds (enzyme cofactors, RNA nucleotides and their precursors or derivatives) that are predicted to be of ancient origin (Breaker, 2012; McCown et al., 2017; Nelson and Breaker, 2017).
evidence: The introduction states this as an observed pattern supported by citations.

claim: Riboswitch ligands exhibit a bias in favor of compounds that are predicted to be of ancient origin.
source: The collection of known riboswitch classes largely sense compounds or ions that are of fundamental importance to organisms from all three domains of life, and these ligands also exhibit a bias in favor of compounds (enzyme cofactors, RNA nucleotides and their precursors or derivatives) that are predicted to be of ancient origin (Breaker, 2012; McCown et al., 2017; Nelson and Breaker, 2017).
evidence: The introduction states this as an observed pattern supported by citations.

claim: The vast majority of undiscovered riboswitch classes are predicted to be exceedingly rare.
source: Unfortunately, the vast majority of these undiscovered riboswitch classes are predicted to be exceedingly rare, and this characteristic is likely to cause difficulties for researchers who seek to identify them.
evidence: The introduction states this as a prediction based on inference from known patterns.

claim: A computational pipeline was developed that first identifies the regions of bacterial genomes that are most likely to serve as transcription templates for structured noncoding RNAs.
source: To address this challenge, we developed a computational pipeline that first identifies the regions of bacterial genomes that are most likely to serve as transcription templates for structured noncoding RNAs (ncRNAs), and then uses comparative sequence and structural analyses to identify novel candidate RNA motifs (Stav et al., 2019).
evidence: The introduction describes the development of their computational method with citation.

claim: The computational pipeline examines only the putative noncoding regions of a given sequenced bacterial genome.
source: Specifically, this approach examines only the putative noncoding regions of a given sequenced bacterial genome, and evaluates each intergenic region (IGR) based on two parameters: (i) percent guanosine and cytidine (GC) nucleotide content and (ii) length in nucleotides.
evidence: The introduction explicitly describes the methodology of the computational pipeline.

claim: For many bacteria, structured ncRNAs are GC-rich compared to other regions of the genome.
source: For many bacteria, structured ncRNAs are GC-rich compared to other regions of the genome (Klein et al., 2002; Schattner, 2002), and the IGRs that serve as synthesis templates for these ncRNAs tend to be much longer than typical bacterial IGRs that contain only an RNA polymerase promoter and/or a protein-specific regulatory domain.
evidence: The introduction cites references supporting this observation about structured ncRNAs.

claim: IGRs that serve as synthesis templates for structured ncRNAs tend to be much longer than typical bacterial IGRs.
source: For many bacteria, structured ncRNAs are GC-rich compared to other regions of the genome (Klein et al., 2002; Schattner, 2002), and the IGRs that serve as synthesis templates for these ncRNAs tend to be much longer than typical bacterial IGRs that contain only an RNA polymerase promoter and/or a protein-specific regulatory domain.
evidence: The introduction states this as an observed characteristic of ncRNA-encoding IGRs.

claim: The current bioinformatics pipeline is based on earlier implementations that were used to discover several novel structured ncRNA motifs.
source: Our current bioinformatics pipeline is based on earlier implementations of this search strategy that were used to discover several novel structured ncRNA motifs (Meyer et al., 2009), including the SAM-V riboswitch class (Poiata et al., 2009).
evidence: The introduction cites previous work that the current pipeline builds upon.

claim: The updated computational pipeline was employed to comprehensively examine the genomes of five bacterial species.
source: Our updated computational pipeline was employed to comprehensively examine the genomes of five bacterial species, which revealed the existence of as many as 70 novel genetic elements, including 30 candidate ncRNA motifs (Stav et al., 2019).
evidence: The introduction describes the application of their pipeline with citation.

claim: The computational pipeline revealed the existence of as many as 70 novel genetic elements, including 30 candidate ncRNA motifs.
source: Our updated computational pipeline was employed to comprehensively examine the genomes of five bacterial species, which revealed the existence of as many as 70 novel genetic elements, including 30 candidate ncRNA motifs (Stav et al., 2019).
evidence: The introduction states the results of applying the pipeline with citation.

claim: Eight candidate riboswitch classes were uncovered in the computational search.
source: Of the eight candidate riboswitch classes uncovered in this search, the most promising was called the 'thiS motif' (Figure 1A) because representatives most commonly reside immediately upstream of thiS genes, which code for a protein that delivers sulfur to the pathway for the production of the thiamin biosynthetic intermediate 5-(2-hydroxyethyl)−4-methylthiazole phosphate (HET-P) (Begley et al., 2012).
evidence: The introduction states the number of candidate riboswitch classes found.

claim: thiS motif representatives most commonly reside immediately upstream of thiS genes.
source: Of the eight candidate riboswitch classes uncovered in this search, the most promising was called the 'thiS motif' (Figure 1A) because representatives most commonly reside immediately upstream of thiS genes, which code for a protein that delivers sulfur to the pathway for the production of the thiamin biosynthetic intermediate 5-(2-hydroxyethyl)−4-methylthiazole phosphate (HET-P) (Begley et al., 2012).
evidence: The introduction states the genomic location pattern of thiS motif RNAs.

claim: thiS genes code for a protein that delivers sulfur to the pathway for the production of HET-P.
source: Of the eight candidate riboswitch classes uncovered in this search, the most promising was called the 'thiS motif' (Figure 1A) because representatives most commonly reside immediately upstream of thiS genes, which code for a protein that delivers sulfur to the pathway for the production of the thiamin biosynthetic intermediate 5-(2-hydroxyethyl)−4-methylthiazole phosphate (HET-P) (Begley et al., 2012).
evidence: The introduction cites a reference for the function of thiS genes.

claim: Other genes associated with thiS motif RNAs appear to code for proteins that participate in the production of HET-P or its fusion to HMP-PP.
source: Other genes associated with thiS motif RNAs appear to code for proteins that participate in the production of HET-P or its fusion to 4-amino-5-hydroxymethyl-2-methylpyrimidine diphosphate (HMP-PP), to ultimately produce the bioactive coenzyme thiamin pyrophosphate (TPP) (Jurgenson et al., 2009).
evidence: The introduction states the functions of other associated genes with citation.

claim: The thiS motif occasionally resides in tandem with TPP riboswitches.
source: An additional clue regarding the function of thiS motif RNAs was derived from the fact that this novel RNA structure occasionally resides in tandem with TPP riboswitches (Stav et al., 2019).
evidence: The introduction states this genomic arrangement pattern with citation.

claim: Tandem arrangements of other riboswitch classes have been shown to function as two-input Boolean logic gates.
source: Tandem arrangements of other riboswitch classes have been shown to function as two-input Boolean logic gates (Sudarsan et al., 2006; Stoddard and Batey, 2006; Lee et al., 2010; Sherlock et al., 2018), suggesting that the genes associated with tandem arrangements of TPP riboswitches and thiS motif RNAs likely respond to concentration changes of two distinct ligands.
evidence: The introduction cites multiple references supporting this functional characteristic of tandem riboswitches.

claim: Genes associated with tandem arrangements of TPP riboswitches and thiS motif RNAs likely respond to concentration changes of two distinct ligands.
source: Tandem arrangements of other riboswitch classes have been shown to function as two-input Boolean logic gates (Sudarsan et al., 2006; Stoddard and Batey, 2006; Lee et al., 2010; Sherlock et al., 2018), suggesting that the genes associated with tandem arrangements of TPP riboswitches and thiS motif RNAs likely respond to concentration changes of two distinct ligands.
evidence: The introduction infers this based on known behavior of tandem riboswitches.

claim: A riboswitch-reporter fusion construct was created by joining a thiS motif RNA representative to a β-galactosidase gene.
source: Previously (Stav et al., 2019), we created a riboswitch-reporter fusion construct by joining a thiS motif RNA representative to a β-galactosidase gene.
evidence: The introduction describes a previous experimental construct with citation.

claim: The riboswitch-reporter construct exhibited robust gene expression in host Bacillus subtilis cells with a deleted thiS gene (ΔthiS).
source: Using this construct, we observed robust gene expression in host Bacillus subtilis cells with a deleted thiS gene (ΔthiS).
evidence: The introduction states an experimental observation from previous work.

claim: The same reporter-fusion construct yields no reporter gene expression in host B. subtilis cells that naturally carry a thiS gene.
source: This same reporter-fusion construct yields no reporter gene expression in host B. subtilis cells that naturally carry a thiS gene.
evidence: The introduction states an experimental observation from previous work.

claim: Most experimentally validated riboswitch classes are composed of distinct, but partially overlapping aptamer and expression platform domains.
source: Most experimentally validated riboswitch classes are composed of distinct, but partially overlapping aptamer and expression platform domains (Barrick and Breaker, 2007; Breaker, 2012).
evidence: The Results section states this as established knowledge with citations.

claim: The thiS motif exhibits an unusual arrangement wherein the predominant secondary structure is an extended hairpin structure that maximizes conventional Watson/Crick base pairing.
source: In contrast, the thiS motif exhibits an unusual arrangement wherein the predominant secondary structure, derived by thermodynamic modeling, is an extended hairpin structure that maximizes conventional Watson/Crick base pairing (Figure 1A, left).
evidence: The Results section describes the structural characteristics of the thiS motif.

claim: The thiS motif structure exhibits all the features characteristic of bacterial intrinsic terminator stems.
source: This structure exhibits all the features characteristic of bacterial intrinsic terminator stems, including an uninterrupted and strong base-paired stem followed by a run of six or more uridine (U) residues (Wilson and von Hippel, 1995; Yarnell and Roberts, 1999).
evidence: The Results section states this structural observation with citations.

claim: The loop of the terminator hairpin in the thiS motif is abnormally well conserved compared to the loop sequences of more typical terminator stems.
source: When evaluating the thiS candidate, however, we noted four features that suggested this terminator stem was peculiar. First, the loop of the terminator hairpin is abnormally well conserved compared to the loop sequences of more typical terminator stems, which are usually irrelevant to the mechanism of transcription termination.
evidence: The Results section describes an unusual feature of the thiS motif structure.

claim: The thiS motif is found in species from two phyla and from several classes within Firmicutes.
source: This unique terminator element is found in species from two phyla and from several classes within Firmicutes (Supplementary file 1, Supplementary file 2).
evidence: The Results section states the phylogenetic distribution of the thiS motif.

claim: Another consensus structural model for the thiS motif is consistent with the comparative sequence analysis data.
source: Second, another consensus structural model was also consistent with the comparative sequence analysis data (Figure 1A, right).
evidence: The Results section describes an alternative structural model.

claim: The alternative thiS motif architecture includes a possible pseudoknot and two major base-paired stems.
source: This architecture, including a possible pseudoknot and two major base-paired stems, disrupts the contiguous terminator stem near the run of U residues, suggesting that mutually exclusive and competing structures and functions might exist for thiS motif RNAs.
evidence: The Results section describes the features of the alternative structural model.

claim: The specialized terminator stems in the thiS motif associate exclusively with genes related to the biosynthesis and utilization of HET-P.
source: Third, these apparently specialized terminator stems associate exclusively with genes related to the biosynthesis and utilization of HET-P, which is a precursor of the coenzyme TPP (Figure 1B).
evidence: The Results section states the genomic association pattern of thiS motif RNAs.

claim: Approximately 30% of the known thiS motif representatives reside immediately downstream of riboswitches that sense and respond to TPP.
source: A fourth feature of thiS motif RNAs is that approximately 30% of the known representatives reside immediately downstream of riboswitches that sense and respond to TPP (Stav et al., 2019).
evidence: The Results section states the frequency of tandem arrangements with citation.

claim: Each associated TPP riboswitch appears to use a terminator stem as an expression platform.
source: Each associated TPP riboswitch appears to use a terminator stem as an expression platform.
evidence: The Results section states an observation about TPP riboswitch structure.

claim: The natural ligand for the thiS motif riboswitch would not be TPP.
source: Due to these tandem arrangements, we speculated that the natural ligand for this riboswitch candidate would not be TPP.
evidence: The Results section states a speculation based on the tandem arrangement.

claim: The ligand for the thiS motif would be a major precursor of TPP (either HET-P or HMP-PP).
source: Rather, it seemed more likely that the ligand would be a major precursor of TPP (either HET-P or HMP-PP), and that each tandem TPP-thiS motif system would function as a two-input Boolean logic gate (Sudarsan et al., 2006; Stoddard and Batey, 2006; Lee et al., 2010; Sherlock et al., 2018) to regulate HET-P production in response to the cellular concentrations of both TPP and one of its biosynthetic precursors.
evidence: The Results section states a speculation about the ligand identity with citations.

claim: Ligand binding by the aptamer in thiS motif RNAs is expected to activate gene expression.
source: Furthermore, if the two secondary structure states called the 'terminator configuration' and the 'aptamer configuration' (Figure 1A) represent the riboswitch 'OFF' and 'ON' configurations, respectively, then ligand binding by the aptamer in thiS motif RNAs is expected to activate gene expression.
evidence: The Results section states an expectation based on structural models.

claim: The vast majority of riboswitches that sense metabolites and control biosynthetic pathways are OFF switches.
source: The vast majority of riboswitches that sense metabolites and control biosynthetic pathways are OFF switches, and thus the accumulation of the metabolite ligand results in reduced expression of the protein products that otherwise would make (or import) more of the desired metabolite.
evidence: The Results section states this as established knowledge about riboswitch function.

claim: It does not make sense that HET-P would turn on its own production when it is already abundant.
source: Although thiS motif representatives associate with genes for the production of HET-P (Figure 1B), it does not make sense that HET-P would turn on its own production when it is already abundant.
evidence: The Results section states a logical inference about metabolic regulation.

claim: The thiE gene is occasionally associated with thiS motif representatives.
source: Finally, we recognized that the thiE gene (coding for thiamin-phosphate synthase) is occasionally associated with thiS motif representatives, suggesting that the RNA motif determines if cellular conditions are suitable to couple the two key precursors of thiamin monophosphate (TMP) to eventually yield TPP.
evidence: The Results section states a genomic association observation.

claim: thiS motif RNAs function as ON riboswitches for the TPP precursor HMP-PP.
source: Taken together, all these bioinformatic observations are consistent with the hypothesis that thiS motif RNAs function as ON riboswitches for the TPP precursor HMP-PP.
evidence: The Results section states a hypothesis based on multiple bioinformatic observations.

claim: A chromosomally-integrated reporter construct carrying a β-galactosidase gene fused downstream of nucleotides encompassing the thiS motif from Clostridium species Maddingley was employed.
source: As an initial test of our hypothesis that HMP-PP is the ligand for thiS motif RNAs, we employed a chromosomally-integrated reporter construct (Stav et al., 2019) carrying a β-galactosidase gene fused downstream of nucleotides encompassing the thiS motif from Clostridium species Maddingley (Rosewarne et al., 2013) (Figure 2A).
evidence: The Results section describes the experimental construct used with citations.

claim: Transformed B. subtilis cells carrying the wild-type riboswitch-lacZ reporter construct exhibited no β-galactosidase activity in response to HMP added to rich (LB) liquid culture media.
source: Transformed B. subtilis cells carrying a transcriptional fusion of the wild-type (WT) riboswitch to a lacZ reporter gene, which was integrated into the amyE locus, exhibited no β-galactosidase activity in response to HMP added to rich (LB) liquid culture media (Figure 2B).
evidence: The Results section states an experimental observation shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Robust β-galactosidase activity is evident in cells co-transformed with the reporter construct and a vector overexpressing the ThiD protein when growth media is supplemented with HMP.
source: In contrast, robust β-galactosidase activity is evident in cells co-transformed with the reporter construct and a vector overexpressing the ThiD protein, but only when growth media is supplemented with HMP (Figure 2B).
evidence: The Results section states an experimental observation shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Reporter gene expression levels are dependent on the concentration of HMP added to the culture medium.
source: Reporter gene expression levels are dependent on the concentration of HMP added to the culture medium (Figure 2C), suggesting that cells take up HMP and use the thiD gene product to add two phosphates to generate excess HMP-PP, which activates lacZ reporter expression by binding to the riboswitch.
evidence: The Results section states an experimental observation shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Cells take up HMP and use the thiD gene product to add two phosphates to generate excess HMP-PP.
source: Reporter gene expression levels are dependent on the concentration of HMP added to the culture medium (Figure 2C), suggesting that cells take up HMP and use the thiD gene product to add two phosphates to generate excess HMP-PP, which activates lacZ reporter expression by binding to the riboswitch.
evidence: The Results section infers this mechanism from the experimental data.

claim: HMP-PP activates lacZ reporter expression by binding to the riboswitch.
source: Reporter gene expression levels are dependent on the concentration of HMP added to the culture medium (Figure 2C), suggesting that cells take up HMP and use the thiD gene product to add two phosphates to generate excess HMP-PP, which activates lacZ reporter expression by binding to the riboswitch.
evidence: The Results section infers this mechanism from the experimental data.

claim: Constructs carrying mutations M1 (G26C) or M2 (C35G) are not activated by HMP addition.
source: Constructs carrying mutations M1 (G26C) or M2 (C35G) (Figure 2A), which alter strictly-conserved nucleotides that are predicted to be part of the pseudoknot structure of the aptamer (Figure 1A), are not activated by HMP addition (Figure 2C).
evidence: The Results section states an experimental observation about mutant constructs.

claim: Construct M3 (U46A, U47A, U48A) exhibits a detectable level of reporter gene expression in LB media alone.
source: Importantly, construct M3 (U46A, U47A, U48A) exhibits a detectable level of reporter gene expression in LB media alone, and this expression is further enhanced by the addition of HMP.
evidence: The Results section states an experimental observation about the M3 mutant.

claim: The M3 construct expression is further enhanced by the addition of HMP.
source: Importantly, construct M3 (U46A, U47A, U48A) exhibits a detectable level of reporter gene expression in LB media alone, and this expression is further enhanced by the addition of HMP.
evidence: The Results section states an experimental observation about the M3 mutant.

claim: The nucleotides at positions 46-48 are involved in forming a strong terminator stem.
source: This result suggests that these nucleotides are involved in forming a strong terminator stem, but that the identities of the nucleotides at these positions are not critical for ligand binding by the putative HMP-PP aptamer.
evidence: The Results section infers this from the M3 mutant behavior.

claim: The identities of the nucleotides at positions 46-48 are not critical for ligand binding by the putative HMP-PP aptamer.
source: This result suggests that these nucleotides are involved in forming a strong terminator stem, but that the identities of the nucleotides at these positions are not critical for ligand binding by the putative HMP-PP aptamer.
evidence: The Results section infers this from the M3 mutant behavior.

claim: B. subtilis cells grown in LB medium are expected to suppress the genes needed to produce both HMP-PP and HET-P.
source: B. subtilis cells grown in LB medium are expected to suppress the genes needed to produce both the pyrimidine moiety HMP-PP and the thiazole moiety HET-P.
evidence: The Results section states an expectation about metabolic regulation in rich media.

claim: Expression of the reporter gene fused to the putative HMP-PP riboswitch is off in LB medium, regardless of the genetic background tested.
source: Thus, as expected, expression of the reporter gene fused to the putative HMP-PP riboswitch is off, regardless of the genetic background tested.
evidence: The Results section states an experimental observation.

claim: WT cells grown in minimal (GMM) medium do not express the reporter gene.
source: Likewise, WT cells grown in minimal (GMM) medium also do not express the reporter gene, presumably because HMP-PP does not accumulate due to its rapid and efficient conversion to the final product, TPP.
evidence: The Results section states an experimental observation with interpretation.

claim: ΔthiS and ΔthiE cells exhibit high levels of reporter gene expression.
source: By contrast, ΔthiS and ΔthiE cells (carrying genetic disruptions of the thiS and thiE genes, respectively) exhibit high levels of reporter gene expression (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The Results section states an experimental observation shown in a figure supplement.

claim: ΔthiS and ΔthiE genetic knock-out strains are predicted to accumulate HMP-PP.
source: These two genetic knock-out strains are predicted to accumulate HMP-PP because they either lack the protein (ThiS) that initiates the production of HET-P, or they lack the protein (ThiE) that fuses HMP-PP to HET-P even when HET-P is available.
evidence: The Results section infers metabolic consequences of the genetic knockouts.

claim: Reporter gene expression is not observed in ΔthiD cells.
source: Reporter gene expression is not observed in ΔthiD cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), despite the fact that these cells should accumulate HMP-P.
evidence: The Results section states an experimental observation shown in a figure supplement.

claim: ΔthiD cells should accumulate HMP-P.
source: Reporter gene expression is not observed in ΔthiD cells (Figure 2—figure supplement 1C), despite the fact that these cells should accumulate HMP-P.
evidence: The Results section infers metabolic consequences of the genetic knockout.

claim: The genetic results strongly indicate that HMP-PP is the ligand for a riboswitch class represented by thiS motif RNAs.
source: Overall, these genetic results strongly indicate that HMP-PP is the ligand for a riboswitch class represented by thiS motif RNAs that turns on gene expression when this ligand is abundant.
evidence: The Results section draws a conclusion from the genetic experiments.

claim: thiS motif RNAs turn on gene expression when HMP-PP is abundant.
source: Overall, these genetic results strongly indicate that HMP-PP is the ligand for a riboswitch class represented by thiS motif RNAs that turns on gene expression when this ligand is abundant.
evidence: The Results section draws a conclusion from the genetic experiments.

claim: The two possible architectures of the thiS motif RNA suggest a mechanism for gene regulation involving the mutually exclusive formation of an intrinsic terminator stem and its competing ligand-bound aptamer state.
source: The two possible architectures of the thiS motif RNA from C. sp. Maddingley (Figure 3A), also observed in other members of this candidate riboswitch class (Figure 1A), suggest a mechanism for gene regulation involving the mutually exclusive formation of an intrinsic terminator stem and its competing ligand-bound aptamer state.

claim: Such transcription control mechanisms for riboswitches have been experimentally validated in the past by using single-round in vitro transcription assays.
source: Such transcription control mechanisms for riboswitches have been experimentally validated in the past (e.g. McDaniel et al., 2003; Mironov et al., 2002; Sudarsan et al., 2003; Wickiser et al., 2005a) by using single-round in vitro transcription assays (Landick et al., 1996) to reveal ligand-dependent modulation of RNA transcript lengths.
evidence: The Results section cites previous work on riboswitch mechanisms.

source: Therefore, we freshly generated HMP-PP from HMP and ATP enzymatically (Figure 3B) by using recombinantly produced ThiD protein.

claim: HMP-PP binding induces RNA polymerase to transcribe past the intrinsic terminator element to yield fewer terminated products and a greater proportion of FL RNAs.
source: These results suggest that HMP-PP binding induces RNA polymerase to transcribe past the intrinsic terminator element to yield fewer terminated (T) products and a greater proportion of FL RNAs.

claim: Construct M4 yields nearly 100% 'FL' transcripts.
source: From the assay data presented, this switching effect is incomplete in vitro, as evident by the fact that construct M4, which carries three nucleotide changes that disrupt the otherwise perfect base pairing of the terminator stem, yields nearly 100% 'FL' transcripts.
evidence: The Results section states an experimental observation about the M4 mutant.

claim: Construct M5 yields transcripts that approximate the length of 'T' RNAs.
source: Construct M5 yields transcripts that approximate the length of 'T' RNAs, which are generated naturally by termination due to the action of the intrinsic terminator stem.
evidence: The Results section states an experimental observation about the M5 mutant.

claim: Incomplete switching by terminator-regulating riboswitches is typical for such assays conducted in vitro.
source: Incomplete switching by terminator-regulating riboswitches is typical for such assays conducted in vitro (e.g. McDaniel et al., 2003; Mironov et al., 2002; Sherlock et al., 2018; Sudarsan et al., 2003; Wickiser et al., 2005a).
evidence: The Results section cites multiple references supporting this observation.

claim: A larger dynamic range for transcription control is likely exploited by this riboswitch in cells.
source: However, it seems likely that a larger dynamic range for transcription control is exploited by this riboswitch in cells, as evident by the robust differences in gene expression for the nearly identical reporter constructs used in this study (Figure 2 and Figure 2—figure supplement 1).

source: Therefore, under thermodynamic equilibrium conditions typically experienced by RNAs subjected to in-line probing reactions, a full-length construct is not expected to bind HMP-PP because the RNA will always favor the terminator configuration ('OFF' state).
evidence: The Results section infers this from thermodynamic considerations.

source: To address this problem, we reasoned that a shorter construct that weakens the terminator stem might permit the aptamer configuration to be adopted.
evidence: The Results section states a hypothesis for experimental design.

claim: An RNA polymerase paused at the run of U nucleotides at the end of the intrinsic terminator element will sequester ~12 nucleotides of the transcript within the protein structure.

However, this construct still failed to exhibit ligand-induced changes in the banding pattern resulting from in-line probing reactions.

claim: Nucleotides involved in forming the putative pseudoknot appear to become more structured upon HMP-PP addition.

These additional mutations eliminate structural modulation by HMP-PP (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B), as would be expected if these highly-conserved sequence and structural features are critical for riboswitch aptamer function.
evidence: The Results section states experimental observations about mutant constructs shown in figure supplements.

claim: A partial HMP-PP binding curve for 52 thiS M3 is consistent with a 1-to-1 interaction between the ligand and the RNA aptamer.
source: Regardless, by quantifying the band intensities at the three sites of structural modulation and by assuming that these values could become zero (or background) upon ligand binding, we generated a partial HMP-PP binding curve for 52 thiS M3 (Figure 5C), which is consistent with a 1-to-1 interaction between the ligand and the RNA aptamer.

claim: The KD value for the 52 thiS M3 variant aptamer construct cannot be greater than 500 μM.

claim: The time scale of in-line probing reactions is much longer than the time scale for the natural genetic decision to take place.

claim: Biochemical assays permit the RNAs to reach thermodynamic equilibrium, which should favor the terminator configuration.

source: As noted above, approximately 30% of the representatives of HMP-PP riboswitches reside in tandem with TPP riboswitches.

claim: The TPP aptamer is always associated with its own expression platform, which is routinely a readily recognizable intrinsic terminator stem.

source: The HMP-PP riboswitch follows each complete TPP riboswitch, and by its unique architecture, carries its own intrinsic terminator expression platform.
evidence: The Results section states an observed pattern in tandem arrangements.

source: To confirm that a tandem TPP and HMP-PP riboswitch system functions with this Boolean logic, we created a tandem riboswitch-reporter fusion construct based on the natural C. lundense RNA (Figure 6A), and examined its function in B. subtilis cells.
